_doc: Completed T-0480 ledger. All 75 frozen-manifest members received a dated source sweep. Unlisted overrides use the documented no-corroboration default; pending is empty.
default_summary: No reliable record in the reviewed repository corpus, exact/variant searches, 1839/1843 Chicago directories, and targeted regional/local histories could be tied to this person by more than the recorded postal name. This is a documented no-corroboration result, not evidence that the person did not exist.

ll_andrews_davi.summary: Retrospective Cook County biography identifies David Andrews in Cook County from 1834 and supports exact-name continuity; the evidence does not establish a specific 1 July 1835 roof.

ll_baldwin_eimer.summary: Elmer Baldwin of La Salle County is a plausible spelling candidate for the postal Eimer Baldwin, but competing geography prevents assertion.

ll_bandle_will_nm.summary: William Bandle of Orland Township is a strong regional exact/similar-name candidate, but Orland geography and later directory continuity do not prove the Chicago postal identity.

ll_comstock_hanford.summary: Comstock Hanford of the Will County/Lockport 1835 steel-plow account is a strong regional candidate; the source does not bridge him safely to the Chicago postal entry.

ll_geo_square.summary: Geo. Square may be a transcription/duplicate relation to George Squire; Joliet is competing geography, so both resident IDs and the candidate relation are preserved.

ll_george_e_walker.summary: A primary 1835 Illinois legislative/land record identifies George E. Walker near Utica; the exact name is strong but competing geography prevents a Chicago identity assertion.

ll_george_squire.summary: George Squire is a plausible Joliet regional candidate and possible relation/duplicate to the Geo. Square postal reading; no merge is asserted.

ll_biakie_a_or_h_p.summary: Later Chicago Andrew Blaikie directory entries are a useful spelling candidate for A. or H. P Biakie, but initials and chronology are insufficient for automatic renaming.

ll_harriet_gridley.summary: A Harriet Gridley regional family record is a plausible exact-name lead, but Ottawa/La Salle geography prevents promoting identity or kinship.

ll_harvey_a_blakesley.summary: Exact-name Harvey A. Blakesley appears in later Chicago directories, supporting Chicago continuity while not backfilling a 1834 occupation or specific roof.

ll_henry_mitchell.summary: An 1883 old-settlers report independently places Henry Mitchell in Chicago wagon-factory work in 1834, strongly corroborating the named Chicago person without establishing a May 1835 address.

ll_henry_s_misner.summary: A dated 1834 Kendall-area record supplies a strong Henry S. Misner regional candidate, but competing geography prevents a Chicago identity assertion.

ll_herman_a_rowley.summary: A later Rowley family genealogy is a possible match, but its 1837 Illinois migration chronology conflicts with the 1835 postal entry and it omits the middle initial; retain unasserted.
